what_its_for: Dofetilide is used to treat certain types of irregular heartbeats (called atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter). It helps your heart beat in a normal, steady rhythm.
how_to_take: Take dofetilide by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Take it at the same times every day (usually every 12 hours). Because this medicine can affect your heart rhythm, you must be started on it in a hospital where doctors can watch your heart closely for at least 3 days.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your kidney function and how your heart responds. The usual dose is between 125 mcg and 500 mcg taken twice a day (every 12 hours). Never change your dose on your own. Your dose may need to be adjusted if your kidneys are not working well.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do NOT take two doses at once to make up for a missed dose. Taking an extra dose could cause a dangerous heart rhythm problem.
storage: Store dofetilide at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking many common medications without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, because many drugs can dangerously interact with dofetilide. Some medicines to avoid unless your doctor approves include: cimetidine (Tagamet), verapamil, ketoconazole, trimethoprim, prochlorperazine, megestrol, and certain antibiotics or antifungals. Avoid grapefruit juice. Do not drink large amounts of caffeine. Tell every doctor, dentist, and pharmacist you see that you take this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: fainting or feeling like you might faint, fast or pounding heartbeat, a fluttering feeling in your chest, dizziness or lightheadedness, shortness of breath, unusual weakness, or swelling in your legs or feet. These could be signs of a serious heart rhythm problem. Also call your doctor before starting any new medicine, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements.
when_it_works: Dofetilide starts working relatively quickly to help control your heart rhythm. However, it may take some time to see the full benefit. Your doctor will monitor your heart with an EKG (electrocardiogram) to check how well it is working and to make sure it is safe for you.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If your kidneys do not work well, your dose will need to be lowered. If your kidney function gets too low, you should not use this medicine at all. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to this medicine and require careful monitoring. Pregnancy: Dofetilide may harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine has not been studied in children and is not recommended for patients under 18 years of age.
